A.P. Moller - Maersk reported a group return on invested capital (ROIC) of 7.3% for 2024, which was below its target of delivering a ROIC above 8.5% over a cycle.

- The reported ROIC of 7.3% for 2024 is the figure as stated in the annual report, distinct from the underlying ROIC, which excludes items affecting comparability and was higher.
- Maersk's stated financial ambition is a ROIC above 8.5% measured over a cycle, so the 2024 reported figure fell short of that yearly benchmark.
- Maersk calculates ROIC as profit after tax plus net financial expenses after tax, divided by the average invested capital for the period.
- Invested capital is defined as total equity plus interest-bearing debt, less cash and cash equivalents (and similar items), so the measure reflects returns generated on the capital employed in the business.

پاسخ کوتاه: اختلاف به این دلیل است که هر یک از این نویسندگان نقطهٔ آغاز پادشاهی کوروش را از زمانی متفاوت شمرده‌اند؛ پیرنیا از سال ۵۵۸ پیش از میلاد، هرودوت از ۵۵۹ و کتزیاس از زمانی پیش‌تر آغاز کرده‌اند. کوروش پیش از گرفتن همدان (فتح ماد در ۵۵۰ پیش از میلاد) حدود هفت سال فرمانروای انشان بود.

توضیح:
- پیرنیا پادشاهی کوروش را از ۵۵۸ پیش از میلاد آغاز کرده و تا ۵۳۰ (مرگ کوروش) ۲۲ سال به دست می‌آید.
- هرودوت مدت را ۲۸ سال نوشته که نشان می‌دهد آغاز را از ۵۵۹ پیش از میلاد گرفته است.
- کتزیاس ۳۰ سال نوشته که یعنی آغاز را از زمانی نزدیک به ۵۵۹ یا پیش‌تر از آن شمرده است.
- کوروش پیش از فتح ماد و گرفتن همدان در ۵۵۰ پیش از میلاد، از ۵۵۸ (یا به روایتی ۵۵۹) فرمانروای انشان بود، یعنی حدود هفت سال.

کسروی (احمد کسروی) - کتاب «کارنامه اران» / «تاریخ مشروطه»: بنا را به «یوسف خان، حاکم محمره از طایفه بدره» (شیخ یوسف بن مردان از خاندان کعب/بدره) نسبت می‌دهد که در دوره محمدشاه قاجار شهر را ساخت و رونق داد.

مقایسه: هر دو روایت بنا را به یک شیخ عرب محلی نسبت می‌دهند، اما مأمور انگلیسی آن را به شیخ مشعشع (مشعشه‌ایان) می‌دهد، در حالی که کسروی بانی را شیخ یوسف خان از خاندان بدره (کعب) می‌داند؛ یعنی در هویت خاندان بانی اختلاف دارند.

پاسخ: به نوشتهٔ بهار، طبق قانون امتیاز نفت شمال اگر کمپانی استاندارد اویل امتیاز را به دولت ایران یا به کمپانی خارجی دیگری واگذار می‌کرد، امتیاز باطل و لغو می‌شد.

نکات پایهٔ این پاسخ:
- در ماده‌ای از قانون امتیاز نفت شمال تصریح شده بود که انتقال امتیاز به دولت ایران یا کمپانی خارجی دیگر موجب بطلان امتیاز است.
- در گفت‌وگوهای بعدی روشن شد که استاندارد اویل می‌خواست امتیاز نفت شمال را با کمپانی نفت جنوب (آنگلو-پرشین) مرتبط و یکسان‌سازی کند؛ یعنی در عمل کارش به نفع همان کمپانی انگلیسی جنوب تمام شود.
- به همین دلیل بود که بهار این امتیاز را در حقیقت تلاشی برای گسترش نفوذ کمپانی نفت جنوب به شمال ایران می‌دانست.

Yes — force may be used. In On Liberty, Mill says a person rushing toward a bridge known to be unsafe may be forcibly stopped, because the danger may be unknown to him and time may not allow a warning; this is justified to prevent him harming himself in ignorance. If there is time to warn him of the risk, only a warning should be given, and he must be left free to decide. This does not violate Mill's liberty principle because the principle protects only actions affecting the individual against his own wishes when he is acting knowingly and voluntarily — interference here is not against his real will, since he is acting in ignorance of danger. Mill also says the principle of liberty does not apply at all to those "behind the age of maturity" — children and young persons below the years of legal responsibility — nor to those incapable of rational self-government, such as people in a state of dependence or backward societies.

The biological assumptions (age at breeding, number of young, lifespan) stayed the same, but Darwin revised the time span from 800 years to 740–750 years and the result from nearly nineteen million to nearly fifteen million elephants.

Mill - On Liberty (1859): The tyranny of the majority extends beyond political measures into society itself — the "tyranny of the prevailing opinion and feeling," where society imposes its own ideas and practices as rules of conduct on those who dissent, penetrating deeply into life and enslaving the soul itself ("social tyranny" is more formidable than political tyranny).

Tocqueville - Democracy in America (1835/1840): The tyranny of the majority reaches beyond government into the mind itself — majority opinion creates an intellectual despotism, shaping thought and controlling minds so completely that dissenters cannot even express their doubts freely.

Comparison: Both agree the danger extends past laws and officials into society, but Mill emphasizes social enforcement of custom and opinion over individual conduct, while Tocqueville stresses the majority's psychological and intellectual control over thought itself.

Darwin is referring to Malthus. According to Malthus's Essay on the Principle of Population, population, when unchecked, increases in a geometrical ratio, while subsistence increases only in an arithmetical ratio. Malthus takes it as a rule that population, if unchecked, doubles every 25 years. This gap between the two rates of increase produces the pressure that Darwin generalizes into the struggle for existence across the animal and vegetable kingdoms.

Malthus - Essay on the Principle of Population: population unchecked doubles every 25 years.
Tocqueville - Democracy in America: population of the United States in 1790 was about 4,000,000, and in 1830 about 13,000,000.
Tocqueville - Democracy in America: he gives a doubling period of 22 years.

The figures bear Malthus out roughly: from 4,000,000 to 13,000,000 in 40 years is a bit more than tripling, i.e. a doubling period of about 40 ÷ log2(13/4) ≈ 23–24 years, close to Malthus's 25 years; Tocqueville himself states 22 years.

The corset, Veblen says, is a mutilation that impairs the wearer's efficiency and wastes her vitality, but this very injury serves as evidence that she is not obliged to work — her husband or family can afford to keep her in evident idleness, so the loss of health is offset by the gain in reputability.

- In the chapter on dress as an expression of the pecuniary culture (The Theory of the Leisure Class), Veblen treats the corset as "substantially a mutilation" that injures the wearer's personal efficiency and health.
- The offsetting gain is reputability: the visible handicap proves the woman's exemption from productive labor, which reflects credit on her household's pecuniary strength.
- It has fallen out of use among women of the very wealthy, oldest leisure class because their status is unquestioned and no longer needs such conspicuous proof.
- It persists among some wealthy groups whose pecuniary standing is newer or less secure, and who therefore still resort to this visible evidence of wasteful exemption from work.

Mill - On Liberty: In the United States, majority feeling makes people of large incomes who would like to live showily afraid to do so, so they do not; the tyranny of the majority through social opinion restrains them.

Veblen - Theory of the Leisure Class: The motive is conspicuous consumption — spending lavishly to display wealth and gain status through pecuniary emulation.

Comparison: Veblen's theory explains the motive (conspicuous display of wealth for social standing) that Mill says the majority feeling in the United States restrains, since showy living would invite the disapproval of the majority.

No, both are invalid under the GDPR.

- A pre-ticked box is not valid consent: consent must be given by a clear affirmative act, and silence, pre-ticked boxes or inactivity do not constitute consent (Recital 32 and Article 4(11), GDPR).
- Consent must also be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous, which a pre-ticked box for marketing profiling fails to satisfy (Article 4(11) and Article 7, GDPR).
- Withdrawing consent must be as easy as giving it, so requiring a signed letter by post when consent was given online with one click is not acceptable (Article 7(3), GDPR).
- The data subject must be informed of the right to withdraw consent at any time before giving consent (Article 7(3), GDPR).

Yes — the retailer's use is caught, but the lab's use is not.

- Article 5(1)(f) prohibits placing on the market, putting into service, and using AI systems to infer emotions of natural persons in the areas of workplace and education institutions.
- The exception in Article 5(2)(f)... more precisely, the prohibition allows emotion recognition only where necessary for medical or safety reasons; monitoring staff mood in shops fits neither.
- Article 2(8) (and Recital 26) excludes AI systems developed and put into service solely for scientific research and development from the Act's scope, so the university lab's research-only use is outside the prohibition.
- Once the retailer deploys the same system to monitor employees' emotions at work, it is a use in the workplace context, so Article 5(1)(f) applies and the deployment is prohibited.

If repair or replacement is impossible or unsuccessful, the consumer can then seek a price reduction (or, in limited cases, a final right to reject). The AI Act uses the definition of 'personal data' from Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (the GDPR), specifically Article 4(1).

That definition says personal data means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person. An identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data, or an online identifier. It also covers identification by reference to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural or social identity of that person.

Digital Markets Act (gatekeeper, first offence): 10% of total worldwide annual turnover
AI Act (prohibited AI practice): 7% of total worldwide annual turnover

Ranked from highest to lowest, the DMA fine (10%) exceeds the AI Act fine (7%), which in turn exceeds the DSA fine (6%).

Digital Services Act - 45 million: average monthly active recipients in the Union, used as the threshold for designating very large online platforms (VLOPs) and very large online search engines (VLOSEs)
Digital Markets Act - 45 million: monthly active end users established or located in the Union, used as one of the quantitative thresholds for designating a core platform service provider as a gatekeeper

The DMA additionally requires, alongside the 45 million end users, that the provider has 10,000 yearly active business users established in the Union for the same core platform service (plus a group-wide EU annual turnover of €7.5 billion or market capitalisation of €75 billion, unless other criteria are met).
